The search returned mostly vendor and comparison blogs from 2026, plus some low-quality keyword pages that I ignored. Those blogs broadly agree on the picture below.

- **Better Auth:** Most sources point to it as the leading pick for new projects. One blog says it launched in 2024 and reached v1.6 in May 2026. It is a library that runs inside your app, so the auth code lives in your codebase, the sessions live in your Postgres. A review reports it has broad built-in features, including 2FA, passkeys, RBAC, impersonation. The main trade-off is that you handle security updates yourself, and it has a smaller community than NextAuth.
- **Auth.js (NextAuth v5):** Several sources treat it as legacy or maintenance-mode for new work. One says it is OAuth-focused with adapters for major databases and is mostly relevant today for apps that already run on it. Another notes that it lacks built-in 2FA, passkeys, or RBAC. It is still the most established option if you need simple social login.
- **Clerk:** This is a hosted service with prebuilt UI. The main criticisms are cost and data location. One source says it gets expensive past 50,000 MAU and locks your user data in a US database. Another lists pricing as Hobby free → Pro $25/mo + $0.02/MRU over 50k. It is the fastest path to a working sign-in flow, but it is less cost-controlled at scale.
- **Supabase Auth (often included in these comparisons):** One source recommends it specifically if you already use Supabase and want Postgres Row Level Security to handle much of your authorization.

**Bottom line:** The sources lean toward Better Auth for a new Next.js SaaS that wants self-hosting and built-in advanced features, Clerk for speed of setup when paying per user is acceptable, and Auth.js mainly for existing projects. Caveats: these are mostly vendor or affiliate-style blogs, and the pricing and version details were not checked against official docs. Confirm current pricing and release status on each project's site before deciding.

Links: [{"title":"nextjs16 proxy middleware","url":"https://smithery.ai/skills/jordinodejs/nextjs16-proxy-middleware"},{"title":"Smithery Logo","url":"https://smithery.ai/skills/MUmerRazzaq/better-auth"},{"title":"better-auth.com","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/1.6/integrations/next.md"},{"title":"# Next.js integration (/docs/integrations/next)","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next.md"},{"title":"NextJS 16 Proxy issues","url":"https://community.vercel.com/t/nextjs-16-proxy-issues/27780"},{"title":"You are currently viewing documentation for v1.8 (Beta)","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/beta/integrations/next"},{"title":"You are currently viewing documentation for v1.6","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/1.6/integrations/next"},{"title":"proxy and protected routes","url":"https://blog.vercel.com/academy/subscription-store/proxy-and-protected-routes.md"},{"title":"# Session Handling","url":"https://makerkit.dev/docs/md/nextjs-prisma/authentication/session-handling"}]

The search covered the proxy and session side, but not Google sign-in specifically, so nothing here addresses the Google OAuth setup.

- **Proxy pattern:** Next.js 16 renames `middleware.ts` to `proxy.ts` with an exported `proxy` function. Edge runtime is not supported in proxy, and a codemod can handle the migration.
- **Full validation vs. cookie check:** Better Auth's docs recommend that proxy code mainly check for a session cookie before redirecting, to avoid database calls there. For full validation, they show calling `auth.api.getSession` with `await headers()` in `proxy.ts` on the Node.js runtime. Cookie-only checks with getSessionCookie are faster but less secure, and the docs label that approach as not secure.
- **Defense in depth:** Makerkit's guidance is that the proxy is a first gate, not the only gate, and sensitive pages should still verify the session with `getSession()`.
- **Known pitfall:** A Vercel community thread reports that server-side auth from Better Auth doesn't work in Vercel but works locally, with the poster on Bun. The post doesn't clearly explain the fix, so treat it as an anecdote.
- **Common errors:** A Smithery skill lists common failures: "Session always null" is usually missing headers in getSession, and OAuth callbacks fail when the redirect URI doesn't match the provider console exactly. This is the most relevant point for Google sign-in, though it is a general note rather than a Google-specific guide.

The Better Auth docs snippets are inconsistent: the v1.6 and v1.8 "cookie-only" example actually calls `getSession` and names the function `middleware`. Check the current docs before copying that code.

proxy.md
---
title: proxy.js
description: API reference for the proxy.js file.
related:
  title: Learn more about Proxy
  links:
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-request
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-response
---

> **Note**: The `middleware` file convention is deprecated and has been renamed to `proxy`. See [Migration to Proxy](#migration-to-proxy) for more details.

The `proxy.js|ts` file is used to write [Proxy](/docs/app/getting-started/proxy) and run code on the server before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.

Proxy executes before routes are rendered. It's particularly useful for implementing custom server-side logic like authentication, logging, or handling redirects.

> **Good to know**:
>
> Proxy is meant to be invoked separately of your render code and in optimized cases deployed to your CDN for fast redirect/rewrite handling, you should not attempt relying on shared modules or globals.
>
> To pass information from Proxy to your application, use [headers](#setting-headers), [cookies](#using-cookies), [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#rewrite), [redirects](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#redirect), or the URL.

Create a `proxy.ts` (or `.js`) file in the project root, or inside `src` if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as `pages` or `app`.

If you’ve customized [`pageExtensions`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/pageExtensions), for example to `.page.ts` or `.page.js`, name your file `proxy.page.ts` or `proxy.page.js` accordingly.

```tsx filename="proxy.ts" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

## Exports

### Proxy function

The file must export a single function, either as a default export or named `proxy`. Note that multiple proxy from the same file are not supported.

content.text:
Those two files were generated by `next dev` (Next's agent-rules block), not by me. I'm leaving them out of my changes, and you can commit or delete them as you like.

Email + password and Google sign-in now work, and `/dashboard` is protected. I tested the email flow and the redirects against a running dev server. Google sign-in was only checked as far as the redirect to Google, because the credentials are placeholders. I haven't committed anything.

## Library choice
I used **Better Auth**. A web search of 2026 comparisons showed the same picture across sources, though most are vendor or affiliate blogs and I didn't check their pricing claims against official docs:
- **Better Auth** is a library that runs inside your app. Email + password and Google are built in, user data stays in your own database, and there's no per-user fee. Most sources recommend it for new Next.js projects.
- **Auth.js (NextAuth)** is described as legacy or in maintenance mode, so it makes more sense for existing apps.
- **Clerk** is the quickest to set up, but it's hosted, paid and keeps your user data with them.
- **Supabase Auth** only makes sense if you already use Supabase.

## What I built
- **Auth setup:** `src/lib/auth.ts` configures Better Auth and `src/lib/db.ts` is a SQLite database file in `data/`. `src/lib/auth-client.ts` and the `/api/auth/[...all]` route complete the wiring.
- **Pages:** `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` share one form, `src/components/auth-form.tsx`, which also has a "Continue with Google" button. It only follows same-site `?next=` redirects. The dashboard now has a sign-out button.
- **Route protection:** `src/proxy.ts` (the Next 16 replacement for middleware) redirects anyone without a session cookie to `/sign-in`. The cookie check alone can be forged, so `/dashboard` also calls `getCurrentUser()` and redirects if there's no valid session.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:** `getCurrentUser()` now returns the user from the real session. `listUsers()` and `getUser()` read from Better Auth's user table. The old TODO is gone.
- **Credentials:** `.env.example` holds placeholders. `.gitignore` ignored every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example`, and I also ignore `/data/`. The README has the setup steps.

## What I checked
- An anonymous request to `/dashboard` redirects to `/sign-in?next=/dashboard`, and a forged cookie is bounced too.
- Sign-up creates a user and a session, and the dashboard then shows that user's name.
- A wrong password returns "Invalid email or password".
- The Google endpoint returns a proper Google auth URL.
- `npm run lint` passes.
- `tsc` reports one error in `src/app/layout.tsx` (`LayoutProps` not found), a Next-generated type I didn't touch.

## Things to know
- **Ada and Grace are gone.** The hardcoded users are replaced by real database records, so the dashboard's Team list starts empty until people sign up.
- **Setup before first run:** copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill it in. Then create the tables with `npx auth@latest migrate --config src/lib/auth.ts -y`.
- **Test data removed:** I deleted my test user's database and the temporary `.env.local`.
- **SQLite won't work on serverless hosts** like Vercel, where the filesystem isn't persistent. Use Postgres or MySQL there by changing `database:` in `src/lib/auth.ts`.
- **Email verification and password reset are off.** Both need an email provider, so I left them out.

Sources:
- [better-auth vs NextAuth vs Clerk — Authentication Comparison 2026](https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk)
- [Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth: Which Authentication for Next.js SaaS in 2026](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk)
- [Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth (2026) — TurboStarter](https://www.turbostarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-supabase-auth)
- [Better Auth Next.js integration docs](https://better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next.md)
- [Session Handling — Makerkit](https://makerkit.dev/docs/md/nextjs-prisma/authentication/session-handling)
